research:
**Rundown: 2026 Marrakech International Film Festival Étoile d'Or**

**Current state (as of 19 Nov 2026)**
- The 23rd edition runs from November 20 to 28 at the Palais des Congrès, Cinéma Le Colisée and Musée Yves Saint Laurent Marrakech. No winner has been announced yet.
- The jury will watch and evaluate the 14 films in the Official Competition before choosing the film that deserves the Étoile d'Or, then it will announce its decision during the festival's closing ceremony on Saturday, November 28.
- The jury is headed by Marion Cotillard. I could not confirm the names of the other jury members. One report says the jury has 9 figures from the international film industry, but I found only Cotillard and Franco-Senegalese director and screenwriter Ramata-Toulaye Sy by name.
- Competition films I could confirm from the results:
  - *Alkebulan* (Morocco/Hungary/Qatar), a world premiere.
  - *Ben'imana* (Rwanda/Gabon/France/Norway), which won the Caméra d'Or at Cannes.
  - *Cairo Shadows* (France/Belgium/Tunisia/Egypt), a world premiere.
  - *Waves of Silence*, a world premiere by Farzad Samsami and a feature debut shot in Morocco and concerned with migrant shipwrecks.
  - *Furies* (Lebanon), by Rami Kodeih.
  - *A Day in the Life of Jo: Chapter Phaedra* by Jacqueline Lentzou, a coming-of-age story that pushes the boundaries of realism.
  - *In Chronicles from the Siege* (Palestine), which won Best First Feature at the Berlinale.
  - *Congo Boy* by Rafiki Fariala (Central African Republic), per a French-language report.
- I could not find *Eklipse* in any result, so I cannot confirm it is in the 14-film lineup.
- The full 14-film list is not in my results, so I cannot confirm the remaining titles.
- The prize is reported as worth USD 50,000 according to the 2026 rules. That figure comes from a single source.

**Scheduled before close**
- Opening film: Jesse Eisenberg's *The Debut*, which will be among 76 films from 39 countries screened at the festival.
- Closing ceremony and winner announcement: Saturday, 28 November 2026.

**Base rate**
- Recent winners: Erige Sehiri's Promised Sky (2025), Scandar Copti's Happy Holidays (2024), and Asmae El Moudir's The Mother of all Lies (2023).
- *Promised Sky* beat 12 other feature films in 2025. The winner came from an African-led project and was a female-directed debut-era feature.
- The festival is a competition for first and second features, so winners are typically early-career films. I did not find winners from earlier years, so I cannot establish a longer base rate.

**Resolution if nothing changes**
- The Étoile d'Or should be announced on 28 November, within the window.
- If the winner is one of the five named options (*Alkebulan*, *Furies*, *Cairo Shadows*, *Waves of Silence*, *Eklipse*), the question resolves to that film. *A Day in the Life of Jo: Chapter Phaedra* is also referenced in the question's options.
- Any other film resolves "Other". This includes *Ben'imana*, *In Chronicles from the Siege*, *Congo Boy*, and *The Debut*-adjacent titles, because they are not in the named list.
- "Other" also applies if the prize is shared or if no winner is named before 1 January 2027.

## Second research pass (base rate, primary source, the case against)
**Base rate (counts from what I could verify)**
- I found 16 winners across the 25 editions from 2001 to 2025. The 2001–2003 winners come from Wikipedia's list, Inch'Allah Dimanche, Go and Gori vatra. AlloCiné lists 2006 to 2014 and 2016, with no winner repeated (The Donor (2016) is the last in its list). Recent winners are 2023, 2024 and 2025.
- 2004–05, 2015 and 2017–2022 are missing from my results, so the rate is incomplete.
- In 2023 the jury awarded the Étoile d'Or to a Moroccan film for the first time in the Festival's history.
- None of the five named options has any prior record.

**Primary source**
- The official site (marrakech-festival.com) returned only its 2023 page. I found no 2026 official winner statement or live competition page.
- The jury was announced on 12 November. Besides Marion Cotillard, it includes Claes Bang, Vicky Krieps, Emma Mackey, Gilles Lellouche, Kaouther Ben Hania, Andrew Haigh, Ramata-Toulaye Sy and Saïd Hamich Benlarbi.
- The winner is due at the closing ceremony on 28 November. Nothing I found suggests a decision has been made.

**Strongest evidence against the rundown's framing**
- **Competition size is disputed.** The rundown says 14 films. A report dated today says one film has withdrawn from the Official Competition and will not be replaced, so it will have 13 films. Deadline, two days ago, still says 14. I could not identify the withdrawn film. If it is one of the named options, the option set is wrong.
- **Eklipse remains unconfirmed.** I found it in no result, so it may be the withdrawn film or may never have been in competition.
- **Alkebulan is confirmed.** It is the second feature by Yassine Marco Marroccu and is in competition.
- **"Other" is large.** Ben'imana, In Chronicles from the Siege and Congo Boy are confirmed competitors and fall under Other. The unconfirmed remainder adds more.
- **Shared prize.** One unreliable source (Grokipedia) says the $50,000 prize is shared equally between the director and producer. That is not a split between films, but a true tie would resolve Other.

**Not found:** the full 13/14-film list; Eklipse's status; the withdrawn film's identity; any official 2026 prize rules; winners for 2004–05, 2015 and 2017–2022; and any first-hand 2026 statement from the festival.
